### What feature or enhancement are you proposing?
Import `tetgen` inside `genesis.utils.mesh.tetrahedralize_mesh` instead of at the top of `genesis/utils/mesh.py`, the same way `pymeshlab` is already imported inside `Mesh.remesh`.

### Motivation
`genesis.utils.mesh` is loaded by `import genesis`, so its top-level `import tetgen` makes tetgen a hard runtime requirement for every user, including rigid-only workflows that never tetrahedralize a mesh. tetgen is AGPL-3.0 (see #890). Downstream projects that build container images around Genesis' rigid solver would like to leave it out of the image, but cannot today: `import genesis` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` without it.

### Potential Benefit
- `import genesis` and rigid scenes work in an environment without tetgen (e.g. `uv sync --no-install-package tetgen`).
- Slightly faster import for users who never tetrahedralize.
- No behaviour change for FEM / PBD users: tetgen stays a declared dependency and is imported on first use.

### What is the expected outcome of the implementation work?
With tetgen not installed, `import genesis`, `gs.init(...)` and building/stepping a rigid scene succeed; tetrahedralizing a mesh (FEM / PBD entities) still works when tetgen is installed.

### Additional information
A one-line PR follows. Making tetgen an optional extra is out of scope here.
new_candidates.title: [Feature]: Import tetgen only when tetrahedralizing, so rigid-only users can run without it

### Discussed in https://github.com/UniversalRobots/Universal_Robots_ROS2_Driver/discussions/2069
Originally posted by **crishoj** November 10, 2026 *Edited: the first version of this post asked why `tool_contact()` sometimes does not detect a contact. The robot's own logs show that it _did_ detect it.* We use `trajectory_until` with `TOOL_CONTACT` on UR5e arms to press bellows suction cups onto vinyl records. The descent is a straight Cartesian move of 17–23 mm at 30 mm/s, executed through the scaled joint trajectory controller. **Setup** - ur_robot_driver / ur_controllers 3.8.0, ur_client_library 2.15.0 (Jazzy), three UR5e, PolyScope 5.26.0 - `tool_contact_controller` is activated before each press and deactivated before the next one **One press, robot side and ROS side** (times in seconds, t = 0 when tool contact is enabled) | t | source | | |---|---|---| | 0.000 | ros2_control | `tool_contact_controller: Tool contact enabled successfully.` | | ~0.50 | robot, 500 Hz recording | the arm stops on the object (TCP speed 30 → 0 mm/s), steps back 0.6 mm and stands still at 2–5 N | | 0.568 | robot log | `tool contact detected` | | 0.784 | ros2_control | `scaled_joint_trajectory_controller: Goal reached, success!` | | 0.788 | trajectory_until | `Trajectory finished successfully, did not trigger until condition.` | | 0.789 | ros2_control | `Cancel tool contact requested.` → `Tool contact disabled successfully.` (0.792) | | ~0.80 | robot, 500 Hz recording | the target joint positions move again; the TCP travels 5.7 mm in ~55 ms (peak 309 mm/s), force 3 → 178 N | | 0.859 | ros2_control | safety mode PROTECTIVE_STOP, `C157A1` | There is no `Tool contact finished successfully.` anywhere in that press. On the press 20 s earlier at the same position it came 0.46 s after enabling, followed by `Got request to cancel goal`. In `external_control.urscript`, `tool_contact_detection()` ends with ``` q = get_actual_joint_positions_history(step_back) movel(q) socket_send_int(UNTIL_TOOL_CONTACT_RESULT_SUCCESS, "script_command_socket") textmsg("tool contact detected") ``` so the robot's log line is written after the result was sent. **How often** - Over about three weeks, 64 of roughly 8,800 picks ended in ROS with `did not trigger until condition` while the object was there. - On one arm we could compare 17 of those with the robot's log: 10 have `tool contact detected` inside the press. - All but the one above were harmless, because the remaining travel to the trajectory's end point was only a few mm. **A second observation, possibly related** `UR_Client_Library: Received 8 bytes on script command interface. Expecting 4 bytes, so ignoring this message` is logged many times a minute. In the log around the press above it appears only between a `Tool contact finished successfully.` and the next deactivation of `tool_contact_controller`, and not at all during or after the press whose result went missing. One press also logged `Tool contact finished successfully.` twice, 2 ms apart. **Questions** 1. Is there a known way for `UNTIL_TOOL_CONTACT_RESULT_SUCCESS` to be sent by the script and not reach `tool_contact_controller`? 2. What makes the robot send two integers on the script command socket in one read, and what happens to a tool-contact result that arrives that way? 3. After a detected contact the script holds the arm in `MODE_TOOL_IN_CONTACT` while the trajectory controller's setpoint keeps advancing. When tool contact is then ended, the arm is servoed to that setpoint in one step. Is there an intended guard for this? (#1251 looks like the same step, seen as a velocity-limit message.) 4. Is there anything we should log on either side to tell a failed send on the robot from a dropped read in the client library? Related: #1251, #1953.
new_candidates.title: `tool_contact`: the robot detects the contact, but the result never reaches `tool_contact_controller`

new_candidates.body:
### Describe the bug

In a headless run, a camera without color output (e.g. `data_types=["distance_to_image_plane"]`) makes every Isaac RTX
RGB camera in the process return all-zero RGB, whichever camera is created first.

`IsaacRtxRenderer.create_render_data` sets the process-wide `/rtx/sdg/force/disableColorRender` to `True` for such a
camera, and a color camera does not set it back when there is no GUI.

### Steps to reproduce

```
uv run python repro_depth_only_black.py                 # [repro] depth_camera=False rgb mean=233.8 max=241 disableColorRender=False
uv run python repro_depth_only_black.py --depth_camera  # [repro] depth_camera=True rgb mean=0.0 max=0 disableColorRender=True
```

```python
import argparse

from isaaclab.app import add_launcher_args, launch_simulation

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--depth_camera", action="store_true", help="Add a second camera that outputs depth only.")
add_launcher_args(parser)
args_cli = parser.parse_args()
args_cli.enable_cameras = True

import isaaclab.sim as sim_utils
from isaaclab.assets import AssetBaseCfg
from isaaclab.scene import InteractiveSceneCfg
from isaaclab.sensors import CameraCfg
from isaaclab.utils import configclass, instantiate

CAMERA_SPAWN = sim_utils.PinholeCameraCfg(focal_length=24.0, clipping_range=(0.1, 20.0))
CAMERA_OFFSET = CameraCfg.OffsetCfg(pos=(2.5, 0.0, 1.0), rot=(0.0, 0.2, 0.0, 0.98), convention="world")


@configclass
class SceneCfg(InteractiveSceneCfg):
    ground = AssetBaseCfg(prim_path="/World/ground", spawn=sim_utils.GroundPlaneCfg())
    light = AssetBaseCfg(prim_path="/World/light", spawn=sim_utils.DomeLightCfg(intensity=2000.0))
    cube = AssetBaseCfg(
        prim_path="{ENV_REGEX_NS}/cube",
        spawn=sim_utils.CuboidCfg(size=(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), visual_material=sim_utils.PreviewSurfaceCfg(diffuse_color=(1.0, 0.2, 0.2))),
        init_state=AssetBaseCfg.InitialStateCfg(pos=(0.0, 0.0, 0.25)),
    )
    rgb_camera = CameraCfg(
        prim_path="{ENV_REGEX_NS}/rgb_camera", height=120, width=160, data_types=["rgb"],
        spawn=CAMERA_SPAWN, offset=CAMERA_OFFSET,
    )


def main():
    import carb.settings

    sim_cfg = sim_utils.SimulationCfg(dt=0.01, device=args_cli.device)
    with launch_simulation(sim_cfg, args_cli):
        sim = sim_utils.SimulationContext(sim_cfg)
        scene_cfg = SceneCfg(num_envs=1, env_spacing=4.0)
        if args_cli.depth_camera:
            scene_cfg.depth_camera = CameraCfg(
                prim_path="{ENV_REGEX_NS}/depth_camera", height=120, width=160, data_types=["distance_to_image_plane"],
                spawn=CAMERA_SPAWN, offset=CAMERA_OFFSET,
            )
        scene = instantiate(scene_cfg)
        sim.reset()
        for _ in range(10):
            sim.step()
            scene.update(sim.get_physics_dt())
        rgb = scene["rgb_camera"].data.output["rgb"].torch.float()
        flag = carb.settings.get_settings().get("/rtx/sdg/force/disableColorRender")
        print(f"[repro] depth_camera={args_cli.depth_camera} rgb mean={rgb.mean():.1f} max={rgb.max():.0f} "
              f"disableColorRender={flag}", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### System Info

- Commit: 5006a8b82
- Isaac Sim Version: 6.2.0.0
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04
- GPU: RTX 5090
- CUDA: 13.0
- GPU Driver: 580.178.04

### Additional context

Workaround: set `/rtx/sdg/force/disableColorRender` back to `False` after the scene is created.

### Checklist

- [x] I have checked that there is no similar issue in the repo (**required**)
- [x] I have checked that the issue is not in running Isaac Sim itself and is related to the repo

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] RGB cameras render color next to a depth-only camera in a headless run, in either creation order.
- [ ] Headless runs with only depth-only cameras keep the `disableColorRender` optimization.

new_candidates.body: ### Description A `ParticleField3DGaussianSplat` with no material bound turns one flat colour after some Play / Stop cycles, and a later Play crashes with `ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`. It reproduces with the public `flowers_1` asset. **Steps** 1. Open `flowers_1.usd` and frame the splat. 2. Play about 3 s, Stop, wait about 6 s. Repeat. 3. After every Stop the log shows `[rtx.scenedb] Gaussian prim loaded`. After some Stop (Stop 1 to 49 in our runs) the splat is one colour, and a later Play crashes. **What we found** - It happens with no material bound. Every crash has the same Aftermath shader, `DistilledMaterialInitAndPack ... ParticleFieldEmissive` (see Logs). - With `--/rtx/hydra/supportMultiTickRate=false`, the splat is not reloaded on Stop, and we saw no flat frame and no crash in runs of 60 and 120 cycles. With the default setting and this cadence, every run crashed. - With multi-tick off, a reload triggered by hiding and showing the prim still crashed once in 44 reloads, on a larger splat. **Questions** 1. Is this a known issue with reloading Gaussian particle fields? 2. Is `supportMultiTickRate = false` the recommended workaround? 3. Is a runtime reload of a `ParticleField3DGaussianSplat` (visibility or active toggle, primvar change) expected to be safe? ### Isaac Sim version 6.0.1 ### Operating System (OS) Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 ### GPU Name NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 (8 GB) ### GPU Driver and CUDA versions Driver 591.86, CUDA 13.1 ### Logs ```txt [Error] [omni.rtx] VkResult: ERROR_DEVICE_LOST [Error] [omni.rtx] A GPU crash occurred. Exiting the application... new_candidates.body:
## Summary

Newton 1.6.1 shipped in Isaac Sim 6.2.0.1 predates Newton's deterministic collision pipeline and solver APIs (merged on Newton main in newton-physics/newton#5041, 2026-11-03). There is currently no supported path to achieve run-to-run determinism with contacts enabled when using the Newton backend from an Isaac Sim script.

## Environment

- Isaac Sim 6.2.0.1 (`nvcr.io/nvidia/isaac-sim:6.2.0.1`)
- Newton 1.6.1 (bundled in `isaacsim.pip.newton`)
- Warp 1.17.0 (`omni.warp.core-1.17.0`)
- MuJoCo Warp 3.12.0
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090
- Driver: 610.57.04
- OS: Ubuntu, kernel 6.8.0-138-generic

## Problem

### 1. `wp.config.deterministic = RUN_TO_RUN` fails to compile

Setting the global Warp deterministic flag before Newton initializes causes a compilation failure in Newton's collision pipeline:

```
newton/_src/geometry/contact_reduction_global.py
```

Error: `"Deterministic mode currently supports consumed-return counter atomics only for atomic_add, got atomic_max."`

Newton's `contact_reduction_global.py` uses `wp.atomic_max` for contact-slot reservation (lines 235, 251, etc. in the bundled 1.6.1 wheel). Warp 1.17 deterministic mode does not support `atomic_max`.

### 2. Solver-only deterministic patch runs but is not bit-identical

Patching `SolverMuJoCo._deterministic = wp.DeterministicMode.RUN_TO_RUN` after Newton initializes (bypassing the collision pipeline compilation) and calling `solver._prepare_generated_kernels()` succeeds, and readback confirms `solver_deterministic=1`. However, three identical runs produce different trajectories:

| Scenario | Metric | Spread (n=3) |
|----------|--------|--------------|
| straight (300 ticks, 1 m) | final position error | 5.1 mm |
| square (3 laps, 12 sides) | final position error | 16.3 mm (30 mm spread) |

For comparison, PhysX GPU produces **spread = 0** (bit-identical) on the same scenarios.

### 3. Root cause: contacts from Newton's non-deterministic pipeline

`MuJoCoSolverConfig` defaults `use_mujoco_contacts=False`, so contacts come from Newton's own collision pipeline, which has no `deterministic` option in 1.6.1. Making the solver deterministic does not help when its contact input is not. Newton's own `test_solver_determinism.py` (bundled in the wheel) runs its rigid-body tests with `disable_contacts=True`.

## What we tried

1. `wp.config.deterministic = wp.DeterministicMode.RUN_TO_RUN` before init -- compile failure (above)
2. Patching `solver._deterministic` after init -- runs but not bit-identical (above)
3. Looking for `NewtonConfig.deterministic` or `MuJoCoSolverConfig.deterministic` -- neither exists
4. Looking for `CollisionPipeline(deterministic=True)` -- not present in Newton 1.6.1

## Current state on Newton main

Newton's main branch (post-PR newton-physics/newton#5041, merged 2026-11-03) documents and implements:

- `CollisionPipeline(deterministic=True)` -- sorts contacts, fingerprint tie-breaking
- Per-solver `deterministic=wp.DeterministicMode.RUN_TO_RUN` as a public constructor argument
- SolverMuJoCo is listed as "CPU only" for determinism (GPU compilation still fails with Warp 1.19; MuJoCo Warp does not yet order contacts/constraint rows, tracked in newton-physics/newton#5042)

The full determinism roadmap is tracked in newton-physics/newton#5049.

## Questions

1. When will Isaac Sim ship a Newton version (>= the one with newton-physics/newton#5041) that exposes `CollisionPipeline(deterministic=True)` and solver `deterministic` constructor arguments?
2. Will `isaacsim.physics.newton`'s `NewtonConfig` or `MuJoCoSolverConfig` gain a `deterministic` field that users can set from scripts, so determinism can be enabled without patching private attributes?
3. `MuJoCoSolverConfig.use_mujoco_contacts` exists (defaults `False`) but does not appear in the public docs. Is enabling it (to route contacts through MuJoCo Warp's own pipeline, bypassing Newton's `atomic_max` path) a supported configuration? If so, does it have accuracy/feature parity with the default Newton contacts?

## Repro

Open-loop TB3 articulation on a triangle-mesh ground plane, velocity drives, 1/60 s dt, 10 substeps. Scenario script and full data at [ycpss91255-docker/isaac#310](https://github.com/ycpss91255-docker/isaac/issues/310). The comparison shows PhysX GPU is bit-identical across runs while Newton is not.

Data filed on Newton's determinism epic: newton-physics/newton#5049 (comment).
new_candidates.title: Newton backend: no supported path to run-to-run determinism with contacts (6.2.0.1)
